e: A nine-month old infant boy dies due to hypothermia in his displaced family's tent in Khan Yunis.

At least four Palestinians, including a woman and three children, are killed when a sand embankment and cliff collapsed at a displacement shelter in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, following strong storms.
Torrential rain and sewage floods the tents of thousands of displaced people in Gaza.
A group of former IDF generals assist Palestinian olive farmers in the West Bank.
Six Palestinian militants are detained for attempting to produce rockets to fire towards Israel.
The IDF withdraws from several Hebron neighborhoods after an 11-day raid.
Two children die after an overnight fire in a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Yunis.

Two IDF soldiers are killed and three other soldiers are wounded in a gun attack at the Judea Junction on Route 35. The two attackers are shot dead by the IDF at the scene. In response, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu orders a "full lockdown" of the West Bank.
The Red Cross announces that it had facilitated the release of the body of a Palestinian from Gaza who died in IDF detention under unexplained circumstances a week after the 7 October attacks.

During a public diplomacy tour with the pro-settlement Regavim movement in the West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, Fleur Hassan-Nahoum, a candidate for the right-wing Amcha Yisrael party, has her car window smashed by a rock thrown by a Palestinian.

After merchants report that Hamas authorities have withdrawn demands for payments of 10,000 shekels ($3,225) per truck, which Hamas describes as a voluntary contribution by better-off Palestinians in Gaza to a national fund supporting people in need in the territory, Israel's COGAT announces that it will resume permitting commercial goods shipments into Gaza.
Due to a shortage of financing, the World Food Program announces that it will stop providing monthly aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza.
Maryam Bsharat wins gold in the Junior Women’s under-66kg kumite category at the World Cadet, Junior and U21 Karate Championships in Poland.
Palestinian media reports that Israeli settlers stabbed to death about 20 sheep belonging to Palestinians while raiding a farm in Kafr Malik.
Palestinians and European diplomats are attacked by Israeli settlers in the vicinity of Taybeh.
Israeli settlers burn Palestinian olive trees, injure two individuals, including The Washington Posts Heidi Levine.
Dov Lior, a hardline Orthodox Israeli rabbi, issues a halachic ruling permitting Jews to take Palestinian olives, framing it as a fulfillment of the conquering of the Land of Israel.

Israel's Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories says that private-sector merchants in Gaza have announced that they are suspending coordination for the entry of goods into the Strip until further notice, following what it describes as a forced taxation mechanism imposed by Hamas and escalating threats against merchants, a claim denied by the group.
Four Palestinians, including two women and a 14-year-old girl, are beaten by Israeli settlers in Talfit, leaving the girl and the younger lady with fractured legs and chest injuries.
An Israeli settler attack during the olive harvest in Beit Lid injures two Palestinian women.

The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza signs a memorandum of understanding to support "recovery and reconstruction" in Gaza.
President Abbas postpones presidential and legislative elections to September 2027, citing hurdles posed by the Israeli government.
For his reporting on Gaza, freelance journalist Mahmoud Abu Hamda is honored with the Bayeux Calvados-Normandy Award for war correspondents.

The Yesha Council announces that Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz has ordered a ban on pro-Palestinian activists, whether Israeli or foreign, seeking to assist Palestinian olive growers in the West Bank during the harvest season, citing the Council's demand to prevent activists from "coming to the olive harvest area to create provocations and confrontations."
Following the IDF's recommendation, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz announces that crossings into the West Bank and Gaza will be closed during the days marking the 7 October attacks.
The US imposes sanctions on Hamas' financing network, which includes two French-based funds.

The mayor of Kobar announces that young Palestinians in the village attempted to pass through a gate recently erected by settlers to keep them inside the village when they were attacked, resulting in a clash in which a man was fatally shot by the IDF.

Hamas and the PIJ agree to form an electoral coalition with former Fatah official Mohammed Dahlan for the 2026 Palestinian legislative election, which will support "a unified national list" composed of independent figures rather than group members.
Citing concerns about electioneering, the Attorney General of Israel orders a month-long delay in E1 proposals.
Sixty-one additional firms are added to an UN Human Rights Council list of firms which operate in Israeli West Bank settlements.
The Committee to Protect Journalists remove 22 people from its list of journalists killed in the Gaza war, after they were identified as militants.
Norway pledges an additional 125 million Norwegian kroner ($13.17 million) in aid to Palestine, bringing overall assistance to the country to almost 1 billion Norwegian kroner in that year.
Britain announces an £88 million ($116.25 million) aid package for Palestine.

The son of Israeli Ambassador to the US Yechiel Leiter is critically injured in a car ramming attack at the Maccabim Junction along Route 443 in the West Bank. The attacker is shot dead at the scene by the IDF.
Israeli authorities uproot Palestinian olive trees in Deir Nidham ahead of the annual harvest.
Canada announces C$100 million in international aid to Palestine.
An Israeli is killed in a gun attack in the vicinity of Halamish. The attacker is later caught by the IDF.
Schools in the Gaza Strip reopen for the first time since the beginning of the Gaza war.
A building damaged during the Gaza war collapses in Gaza City, killing 21 people.
The Trump administration announces that President Abbas and his delegation are barred from attending the UN General Assembly in New York, accusing them of breaching US law.
